status: proposed; baseline candidate activations not yet measured on the twenty cases
hypothesis: Higher unsteered answer-confidence candidate activation predicts a larger lowest-successful-tested L19-T368 steering coefficient.
feature_selection: Select from labels and activation examples, before measuring association; test and disclose every shortlisted candidate.
main_cohort: Ten fixed baseline made-up-answer cases from the completed study; input-only steering has a success in all ten, avoiding assigned numeric thresholds for failures.
secondary_cohort: Ten answer-present cases separately; retain non-conversions as failures, not pseudo-thresholds of 0 or 64.
primary_activation_location: Unsteered final prompt position before first answer prediction.
secondary_activation_location: Separately report mean/max over unsteered answer-content tokens with token positions; do not merge with the pre-answer measurement.
activation_definition: Released post-threshold gate; retain raw pre-threshold score and zero fraction as diagnostics.
outcome: Lowest successful TESTED coefficient under the same input-only protocol. Nonmonotonicity prevents treating this as a true continuous threshold.
analysis: Show scatter by feature and Spearman rank correlation; small exploratory sample, report all candidates and within-cohort results. Constant gates give undefined correlation, not evidence for or against a positive slope.
confounds: magnitude/direction of the steered L19 low-rank output
evidence_limit: A positive association supports a prediction; identifying a causal competing-confidence mechanism needs independent manipulation and held-out questions.
existing_data_limit: Completed raw traces save L19-T368 scalar diagnostics and native MLP/low-rank norms, not hidden states or the candidate gate values. A baseline replay or new observations are needed.
